def: A vector with one entry equal to 1 and all others 0, identifying a single vocabulary item and carrying no notion of similarity.
A dense, learned vector of a few hundred numbers that represents a word, token or other discrete item so that similar items lie close together.
A matrix with one row per vocabulary item whose rows are looked up by index and trained like any other weights.
Reusing the input embedding matrix, transposed, as the output layer of a language model to save parameters.
The idea that words occurring in similar contexts have similar meanings.
The fixed number of words on either side of a word that count as its context.
A table counting how often each pair of words appears within a context window of each other.
The log of how much more often two words occur together than they would if they were unrelated.
The cosine of the angle between two vectors, equal to their dot product once both are scaled to length one.
A family of small models that learn word vectors by predicting words from their neighbours or neighbours from words.
The word2vec variant in which the centre word is used to predict each word in its context window.
Training word2vec by telling real (word, context) pairs from randomly drawn noise pairs instead of normalising over the whole vocabulary.
Randomly discarding very frequent words while reading a corpus, which speeds training and improves vectors for rarer words.
Word vectors with one fixed vector per word regardless of the sentence it appears in.
Vectors computed for each occurrence of a word from the words around it, so the same word can get different vectors.
